add.title: Social News 16/1 — Separate jails proposed for transgender, gay prisoners
add.summary: VietnamNet (16 Jan 2015) reports a proposal by the Social, Economic and Environmental Institute to Vietnam's Ministry of Public Security to house homosexual and transgender prisoners in jails separate from the general prison population, to protect them from sexual harassment; the institute cited US California statistics that 67% of homosexual and transgender prisoners had suffered sexual harassment and a 2014 survey finding that most transgender prisoners wanted separate jails. Critically for the placement lane, the institute stated that under Vietnam's then-current prison infrastructure transgender prisoners could only be held in solitary confinement or mixed with the general population — i.e. no housing wing matched to the prisoner's gender identity existed — and asked that prisoners be allowed to determine their own gender identity. No enacted outcome or newer documented placement practice was found in the two search rounds conducted.
